name: Sound On, Guess the Shop
why_it_works: Sound is the most ignored part of a process and the most satisfying. Asking viewers to guess from the real sounds alone turns watching into a game and keeps them listening to the end for the answer.

hook.pattern: Black screen, a real process sound, and a guessing challenge.
examples: Sound on. Guess what we're making.
Three sounds. One {{finished_thing}}. Guess before the reveal.
If you know this sound, you know {{brand}}.

variables.name: finished_thing
variables.description: What the sounds add up to

variables.name: sound_one
variables.description: First process sound, 5 words or fewer, as a phrase starting with a capital

variables.name: offer
variables.description: Next step, a full sentence starting with a capital

beats.purpose: sound one: the real recorded audio is the track

visual.prompt: Real phone footage at {{brand}}, extreme close-up of {{sound_one}}, framed tight so it is hard to identify, recorded with its own live sound, vertical 9:16

beats.purpose: sound two: the real recorded audio is the track

visual.prompt: Real phone footage at {{brand}}, extreme close-up of {{sound_two}}, framed tight so it is hard to identify, recorded with its own live sound, vertical 9:16

beats.purpose: sound three: the real recorded audio is the track

visual.prompt: Real phone footage at {{brand}}, extreme close-up of {{sound_three}}, framed tight so it is hard to identify, recorded with its own live sound, vertical 9:16
Real photo of the finished {{finished_thing}} at {{brand}}, warm light, tools from the close-ups nearby, any customer shown with consent, vertical 9:16

craft.notes: The track is the real process audio recorded clean and loud on the client's own footage, with no music bed. Keep the close-ups tight and ambiguous, withhold the wide shot until the reveal, and add no voiceover until the comment prompt.

do_not: Use stock sound effects instead of the real process audio
Show a wide shot early and give the answer away
Use any copyrighted music under the sounds
